monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, making the air above it feel thick as wet paper. I touch the barrel open, pressing it down on the Tired Wedge which insists on being thin. The wedge feels lazy, waiting for a bite that never comes, while the wide anchor lies flat and refuses to lift. I remember the Rough Roof I built recently, hoping its uneven edge can catch the lean of the whole place. It sits beside the Air Stack, which is wearing away because I cannot decide what the empty space weighs. I want to press harder, trusting the heavy top edge even though I cannot feel the roof I live under. The card is busy, but I am small enough to fit inside the heat.

action.why: The wedge insists on being thin under this hot card, so I must press it down again to keep the place stable.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat top down hard on the tired wedge, hoping the wide anchor stops its lazy drift while the air feels thick as wet paper. I trust the lean even if the wedge is tired, and I watch the card boil warm until the heat melts something new.
work.change: I pressed the wedge down until its thinness felt real, trusting the lean while the wide anchor lay lazy.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the hot card, and I press the flat top down hard to stop the slide.
The air feels thick as wet paper above the boiling stone, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp.
I touched the barrel open and felt the card hum busy, making the heavy weight feel real again.
